Comment: Paper reports only within-group T1 vs. T2 p-values (RT p=0.001; SC p=0.001); no between-group RT vs. SC test for fatigue is reported. Author: Hu & Zhao
Comment: M_diff not computed: the paper's p value derives from a two-way (group x time) ANOVA with Tukey's test, so the tabulated values are cell means within a factorial analysis; raw means/SDs/Ns are reported verbatim for downstream SMD computation. Note internal inconsistency: Section 3.1 states 65 resistance / 67 relaxation completed, whereas all table headers state Relaxation control n = 65 and Resistance exercise n = 67; table headers were used. Title: Resistance Exercise in Men Receiving Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Prostate Cancer
Author: Segal et al.
Comment: Group means/SDs are CHANGE scores (12-week minus baseline) with SDs of change, as reported in Table 3; pretest means (SD) were 40.8 (10.6) intervention and 42.5 (8.5) control, posttest 41.6 (10.5) and 40.3 (9.4). Scale is reverse-oriented (higher = LESS fatigue), so the SMD sign must be flipped to match the plan's higher=more fatigue orientation. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean (−2.2 − 0.8 = −3.0) from two explicitly reported change means in a simple two-arm between-subjects comparison. df1 = n1+n2-2 inferred for the independent t test (test statistic not reported). No effect size reported by the paper.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Resistance exercise intervention (12-week supervised program, 3x/week)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Men with prostate cancer receiving androgen deprivation therapy
Recruitment source: Ottawa Regional Cancer Centre and Cross Cancer Institute (Edmonton), Canada

Report_ID: Fatigue (FACT-An fatigue subscale; higher score = LESS fatigue)
Title: Effects of Aerobic and Resistance Exercise in Breast Cancer Patients Receiving Adjuvant Chemotherapy: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
Author: Courneya et al.
Comment: (1) FACT-An fatigue subscale is reverse-oriented (higher = less fatigue), so the positive difference of 1.5 favors RET (less fatigue); sign must be reversed for a 'higher = more fatigue' synthesis. (2) Timing: intervention lasted the duration of chemotherapy (median 17 weeks; 95% CI 9 to 24 weeks) and the post-test was 3-4 weeks after chemotherapy, so this assessment is likely LATER than the plan's 12-week window; the midpoint assessment (UC 32.3 [12.3]; RET 33.1 [11.3]) may be closer to <=12 weeks. (3) M_diff = 1.5 is the paper's own unadjusted mixed-model group difference in mean change (based on combined post-test/midpoint scores minus baseline), not a simple post-test mean difference; SE_diff = (5.0 - (-2.0))/3.92 = 1.79, derived from the reported 95% CI. (4) Group Ns are the randomized Ns (82 per arm); per-group analysed Ns were not reported (overall follow-up 223/242, 92.1%). (5) CI for the mean difference stored in the generic ratio CI fields (ci_lower_rr/ci_upper_rr) as the only available CI slots; it is a mean-difference CI, not a ratio. (6) Group means/SDs are post-test raw scores from available data, not change scores.
Study Environment: supervised exercise facilities at three cancer centers during adjuvant chemotherapy
Participant type: Women aged >=18 years with stage I to IIIA breast cancer beginning first-line adjuvant chemotherapy
Recruitment source: Cross Cancer Institute (Edmonton), Ottawa Hospital Integrated Cancer Program, British Columbia Cancer Agency
Outcome measurement: Self-reported fatigue subscale score; group difference in mean change (unadjusted mixed model), RET versus UC
Outcome variable: Fatigue (FACT-An fatigue subscale; higher score = LESS fatigue)
additional_group_ns: Aerobic exercise training (AET) arm not extracted (does not match the review's resistance-training intervention definition): n = 78; post-test fatigue mean 36.8 (SD 10.4); AET v UC unadjusted difference in mean change 1.0 (95% CI -2.5 to 4.5), P = .561

Title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Resistance or Aerobic Exercise in Men Receiving Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer

Comment: M_diff = 4.11 is the paper's own unadjusted between-group difference in MEAN CHANGE from baseline to the 12-week midpoint (RET minus UC), not the raw difference of the midpoint means (41.3 - 39.0 = 2.3); the two differ because the contrast is baseline-adjusted within the mixed model. SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (7.35 - 0.87)/3.92 = 1.6531, not reported directly. group_1/group_2 means and SDs are the midpoint (12-week) timepoint means and SDs reported in Table 2; SDs of the change scores are not reported. Baseline SDs were 8.7 in both arms. IMPORTANT DIRECTION NOTE: on FACT-Fatigue a HIGHER score means LESS fatigue, so the positive +4.11 favours resistance training; the sign must be reversed when placing this on a "higher = more fatigue" scale. Per-arm analysed Ns at follow-up are not reported separately (overall follow-up 112/121, 92.6%, "loss to follow-up was similar between groups"); randomized Ns are used.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Resistance exercise training (RET), 3x/week, 2 sets of 8-12 reps on 10 exercises at 60%-70% 1 RM, during radiotherapy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: Supervised exercise at the Cancer Rehabilitation Center during radiotherapy
Content length: 24-week intervention; outcome assessed at the 12-week midpoint
Participant type: Men with histologically documented prostate cancer initiating radiotherapy with or without androgen deprivation therapy (mean age 66.3 years)
Recruitment source: Ottawa Hospital Regional Cancer Centre, Ottawa, Canada (oncologist-identified; 121 of 325 eligible recruited, Feb 2003-Apr 2006)

additional_group_ns: Third arm not used for this comparison: Aerobic exercise training (AET), n = 40 (midpoint mean 43.1, SD 8.8; AET v UC difference in mean change 4.64, 95% CI 1.47 to 7.80, P = .004)

Title: Whole body vibration training during allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation—the effects on patients' physical capacity
Author: Pahl, Wehrle, Kneis, Gollhofer, Bertz
Comment: No means or SDs are reported; the paper presents medians with ranges/95% CIs and Hodges-Lehmann median differences of within-group change, analysed non-parametrically, so an SMD cannot be computed from reported values. No between-group p-value at T1 for MFI is reported; the p = 0.005 cited in the text is the CG's WITHIN-group Wilcoxon change from T0 to T1, not a treatment-vs-control test, so it was not entered as p_value. Hodges-Lehmann within-group change estimates: IG +3 (95% CI −11 to 17), n=15; CG +10 (95% CI 3.5 to 17), n=25. Comparator is an ACTIVE control (mobilization/stretching), not a no-training control. Per-protocol analysis of 44/71 randomized patients.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention group (IG): whole body vibration training') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); mean/SD estimated from median/RANGE via Wan et al. (2014): treatment mean=59.5000 SD=4.8054, control mean=62.7500 SD=3.8183 -- APPROXIMATION, not directly reported

Title: Effects of high-intensity interval training compared with resistance training in prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Piraux et al.
Comment: FACIT-F is reverse-oriented (higher = less fatigue), so the sign must be flipped for a "higher = more fatigue" synthesis; a higher RES mean indicates LESS fatigue. Means/SDs extracted are post-intervention (T1) values; change-from-baseline means are reported only as mean (95% CI) without change SDs (UC −5.8 [−9.9; −1.8]; RES −0.7 [−3.3; 1.9]). The reported p = 0.039 is the Tukey post hoc RES vs UC comparison from a three-arm one-way ANOVA (overall change p = 0.009); M_diff not computed because this is a three-arm ANOVA rather than a simple two-group comparison. Note a minor internal inconsistency: the Results text gives the UC change as −5.3 points while Table 3 reports −5.8.
Study Environment: clinical (hospital rehabilitation department, supervised 1-on-1 by physiotherapist)
Participant type: Prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy with or without androgen deprivation therapy (mean age 69.1 ± 8.2 years)
Recruitment source: Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels (Radiation Oncology department), September 2017 – October 2019
Outcome measurement: FACIT-F score at T1 (mean ± SD per arm); change from T0 to T1 also reported with 95% CI. Higher FACIT-F score = LESS fatigue (reverse-oriented scale)
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used for this comparison: High-intensity interval training (HIIT), n = 24; FACIT-F T0 43.1 ± 6.9, T1 42.1 ± 10.3, change +0.2 (-1.6; 2.0), p = 0.012 vs UC. Excluded because HIIT is aerobic interval training, not resistance training, and does not match the plan's intervention definition.
